newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ZALAKERAMIA OWNERS APPROVE CAPITAL RAISE.
newsitem.headline: ZALAKERAMIA OWNERS APPROVE CAPITAL RAISE.

text.p: Shareholders of Hungarian tile maker Zalakeramia gave their approval for the issue of new stocks at an extraordiary shareholders meeting on Wednesday.
The company will privately issue new shares between 900,000 and 1,200,000 units, board member Sandor Jellen told Reuters.
"The board was mandated to decide the timing of the issue," he said. "But it will be done in the most appropriate time."
He did not say at what price the shares would be offered.
Credit Suisse First Boston and Raiffeisen Zentral Bank will act as lead managers in the transaction.
Zalakeramia will spend the money it raises to finance its planned acquisitions, two of which are already completed.
The company announced earlier this month that it acquired a majority stake in Hungarian tile maker Pietra Rt.
The Pietra deal follows the acquisition of a 79.3 percent stake in Croatia's Inker ceramics factory. This deal was signed on February 28.
Zalakeramia said in mid-March it began to tap the 20 million German mark bridging credit line to which it resorted to finance the Inker deal which was completed before the capital increase.
The new shares, in the form of Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs), will be traded on the SEAQ in London.
Zalakeramia shares closed unchanged at 8,300 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
